package_info.why_malicious: The package contains code that intentionally disrupts or sabotages web applications if they are deployed on unauthorized domains, effectively acting as a kill-switch to prevent use outside an allow-list. This is a form of retaliatory or vigilante malware, as it damages user systems based on domain checks.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (browser execution of the web app)
execution_context.file_location: main JavaScript bundle (injected by the package)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code checks if the application is running on an unauthorized domain and, if so, erases the entire web page content by setting document.body.innerHTML to an empty string, effectively breaking the application for end users.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code actively sabotages the application if it detects the domain is not on an allow-list, which is a clear sign of intentional disruption.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages should not contain logic that disables or destroys the application based on the deployment environment. Legitimate code should not erase the UI for users based on domain checks.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Domain checks are sometimes used for licensing or feature gating, but should never result in destructive actions like blanking the UI.
key_indicators: Environment variable checks tied to sabotage

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is bundled into the web application via the npm package.
attack_chain.leads_to: Code executes in the browser at runtime.

attack_chain.action: At runtime, the code checks the domain and environment variables.
If the domain is not on the allow-list and NODE_ENV is 'production', the code erases the web page content.
attack_chain.leads_to: Application is rendered unusable for end users.

behavioral_signatures: Runtime domain allow-list checks in frontend code
Environment variable gating tied to sabotage
file_indicators: Presence of code that checks document.domain against a hardcoded list
References to VUE_APP_SECRET_KEY and NODE_ENV in frontend code
network_indicators: None (no network exfiltration in this snippet, but could be combined with others in similar attacks)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan JavaScript bundles for code that checks document.domain against a hardcoded allow-list and performs destructive actions (such as blanking the UI) if the domain is not allowed. Flag packages that manipulate the DOM in this way, especially if tied to environment variables or production checks. Review any package that includes sabotage logic based on deployment context.
